name: ShowPass
tagline: Concert and match tickets, where a stadium sells out in the first five minutes
summary: ShowPass sells tickets for concerts, comedy and cricket: storefront, virtual waiting room, login, event catalogue, seat maps, seat inventory and holds, checkout, payments, QR ticket issuance and notifications. When a stadium tour goes on sale at noon, thirty times a normal hour's fans arrive in the first minutes. A waiting room that lets everyone in at once, double-sold seats and 'paid, no ticket' keep coming back.

tour.headline: The waiting room keeps queue positions in memory, so one crash at the drop lets every fan in at once; a durable queue costs 14 hours.

satd: queue positions live in process memory
rebuilds the map from every seat row per request
release holds when checkout fails instead of a 10-minute cron
per-account limits and bot rate limits
retry creates a second QR code

incidents.title: Waiting room restart let 3 lakh fans in at once
incidents.desc: Five minutes into a stadium tour on-sale the waiting room restarted, lost every queue position and let all fans into checkout together.
whys: Everyone was admitted together
Queue positions were lost when the waiting room restarted
The waiting room keeps queue positions in memory
incidents.fix: Closed the sale and reopened it an hour later.
incidents.lesson: Fans who queued fairly lost their place.

incidents.title: Stadium seat map took 40 seconds to load
incidents.desc: The 60,000-seat stadium map took 40 seconds to load at the drop and many fans gave up.
whys: The seat map was very slow
Each request rebuilt the map from 60,000 seat rows
The seat map is built from every seat row on each request
incidents.fix: Showed a block picker before the seat map.
incidents.lesson: The block picker still loaded the full map.

incidents.title: Same seat sold to two fans
incidents.desc: Seat C-14-22 was sold to two fans who checked out in the same second; one was turned away at the gate.
whys: Two fans hold tickets for one seat
Both checkouts saw the seat as free
Seat sales check and mark seats sold without a lock
incidents.fix: Upgraded one fan to a better seat.

incidents.title: Seats shown sold out while 2,000 were free
incidents.desc: Fans saw 'sold out' for 10 minutes while 2,000 seats sat in abandoned holds.
whys: Fans saw 'sold out' with seats still free
Abandoned holds were released only every 10 minutes
Seat holds are released only by a cron job every 10 minutes
incidents.fix: Ran the release job by hand.
incidents.lesson: Promoters saw it on social media first.

incidents.title: Fans charged but no ticket issued
incidents.desc: 900 fans were charged but got no tickets because payment confirmations arrived after their holds expired.
whys: Fans paid without getting tickets
Payment confirmations arrived after the hold expired
Payments are never reconciled with issued tickets
incidents.fix: Refunded the fans from a manual report.

incidents.title: Bots bought 40% of front-row tickets in 2 minutes
incidents.desc: Scripts placed hundreds of checkouts per second and took most front-row seats, which appeared on resale sites within an hour.
whys: Bots took the best seats
Scripts placed hundreds of checkouts per second
There is no per-account purchase limit or bot rate limit
incidents.fix: Cancelled orders from obviously scripted accounts.
incidents.lesson: Cancelling after the sale angers real fans too.

incidents.title: Fans received two different QR codes for one seat
incidents.desc: Ticket issuance was retried after a slow response and created a second QR code; the gate rejected one of them.
whys: Two QR codes for one seat
Issuance was retried and created a second ticket
Ticket issuance is retried without an idempotency key
incidents.lesson: Fans did not know which code was valid.

incidents.title: Checkout failed and seats stayed held for 10 minutes
incidents.desc: When payments failed, the seats stayed held for 10 minutes, so other fans could not buy them.
whys: Seats stayed held after failed payments
Failed checkouts did not release their holds
Seat holds are released only by a cron job every 10 minutes
incidents.fix: Ran the release job every 5 minutes.
incidents.lesson: Five minutes is an eternity at a drop.

incidents.title: Queue positions lost after a waiting-room deploy
incidents.desc: A deploy during a comedy on-sale restarted the waiting room and every fan lost their position.
whys: Fans lost their queue positions
The waiting room restarted during the deploy
The waiting room keeps queue positions in memory
incidents.lesson: A crash does not respect a freeze.

incidents.title: Seat map timing out for the stadium show
incidents.desc: The seat map timed out for 6 minutes at the second-date on-sale.
whys: The seat map timed out
Every request rebuilt the full map
The seat map is built from every seat row on each request
incidents.fix: Added servers to the seat map service.

incidents.title: Double-sold seats in block C
incidents.desc: Fourteen seats in block C were sold twice during a cricket on-sale.
whys: Seats were sold twice
Concurrent checkouts each saw the seats as free
Seat sales check and mark seats sold without a lock
incidents.fix: Moved the second buyers to other blocks.

incidents.title: Login failing with 'too many connections' at 11:59
incidents.desc: A minute before the drop, logins failed because each login opened its own database connection.
whys: Fans could not log in before the drop
Each login opened its own database connection
Login opens a new database connection for every request
incidents.lesson: The database ran out of memory instead.

incidents.title: Paid, no ticket for 700 fans
incidents.desc: Another on-sale left 700 fans charged without tickets after late payment confirmations.
whys: Fans were charged without tickets
Late confirmations were ignored after holds expired
Payments are never reconciled with issued tickets
incidents.fix: Issued tickets by hand where seats remained.

incidents.title: Bot traffic doubled checkout load at the drop
incidents.desc: Scripted checkouts doubled the load on checkout and inventory in the first minute.
whys: Checkout slowed for everyone
Bots sent hundreds of requests per second
There is no per-account purchase limit or bot rate limit
incidents.fix: Blocked a list of IP addresses.
incidents.lesson: The bots changed addresses within minutes.

incidents.title: Seat map shows held seats as sold
incidents.desc: Fans saw large grey blocks of 'sold' seats that were only held by abandoned carts.
whys: The seat map showed seats as sold
Holds from abandoned carts were still active
Seat holds are released only by a cron job every 10 minutes
incidents.fix: Showed held seats in a different colour.
incidents.lesson: A colour does not free the seat.

incidents.title: Duplicate QR codes after an issuance retry
incidents.desc: Issuance retries during a busy on-sale created second QR codes for 200 tickets.
whys: Fans got two QR codes
A retried issuance created a new ticket
Ticket issuance is retried without an idempotency key

incidents.title: Ticket emails delivered 2 hours late
incidents.desc: Ticket confirmation emails arrived two hours after purchase; fans flooded support.
whys: Fans did not get ticket emails
Emails were sent inline and dropped under load
Ticket emails are sent synchronously without a queue
incidents.lesson: Fans thought their payment had failed.

incidents.title: Payments taken without tickets on Saturday's drop
incidents.desc: Fans charged on Saturday have no tickets; nothing has matched the payments yet.
whys: Fans were charged without tickets
Confirmations arrived after holds expired
Payments are never reconciled with issued tickets

incidents.title: Bots took the front rows again
incidents.desc: Most front-row seats for the second show went to scripted accounts within a minute.
whys: Bots took the front rows
Scripts bought faster than fans
There is no per-account purchase limit or bot rate limit

incidents.title: Waiting room admitted everyone after a crash
incidents.desc: The waiting room crashed at 12:03 today and admitted every fan at once; checkout and inventory are overloaded.
whys: Everyone was admitted at once
Queue positions were lost in the crash
The waiting room keeps queue positions in memory

debts.title: Keep waiting-room positions in a durable queue
debts.desc: Store queue positions in a durable store shared by all waiting-room servers so a crash or deploy never loses them.
debts.cause: The waiting room keeps queue positions in memory

debts.title: Precompute the seat map and serve it cached with live updates
debts.desc: Precompute each venue's seat map once and serve it cached, sending only availability changes to fans.
debts.cause: The seat map is built from every seat row on each request

debts.title: Sell seats with a row-level lock
debts.desc: Check and mark a seat as sold under a row-level lock so two concurrent checkouts cannot both take it.
debts.cause: Seat sales check and mark seats sold without a lock

debts.title: Expiring seat holds, released the moment checkout fails
debts.desc: Each hold carries its own expiry and is released immediately when payment fails or the fan leaves, instead of waiting for a cron job.
debts.cause: Seat holds are released only by a cron job every 10 minutes

debts.title: Reconcile payments with issued tickets every 5 minutes
debts.desc: Match every captured payment with an issued ticket; issue it if seats remain or refund automatically.
debts.cause: Payments are never reconciled with issued tickets

debts.title: Per-account purchase limits and bot rate limits
debts.desc: Limit tickets per account and card, and rate limit checkouts per account and device so scripts cannot outrun fans.
debts.cause: There is no per-account purchase limit or bot rate limit

debts.title: Idempotency key for ticket issuance
debts.desc: Issue at most one ticket per order line: a retry returns the ticket already issued.
debts.cause: Ticket issuance is retried without an idempotency key

debts.title: Use a shared connection pool for login
debts.desc: Login borrows from a shared, bounded connection pool instead of opening a new database connection per request.
debts.cause: Login opens a new database connection for every request

debts.title: Send ticket emails through a durable queue
debts.desc: Checkout publishes ticket emails to a durable queue; workers send them with retries.
debts.cause: Ticket emails are sent synchronously without a queue

debts.title: Timeouts on payment gateway calls in checkout
debts.desc: Give every gateway call a strict timeout so a slow gateway frees checkout threads.

debts.title: Serve cached event pages from the edge
debts.desc: Event and venue pages are served cached at the edge for a minute instead of being rendered for every fan.

debts.title: Load test the drop at 30x before every stadium on-sale
debts.desc: Replay a stadium on-sale at 30 times a normal hour against staging, including bots and failed payments.

debts.title: Use IST for on-sale start times
debts.desc: On-sale times are stored and checked in IST.
